text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- Social Democrat chief whip Peter Kostelka says 66 hours of total shop opening hours as opposed to the previous 60 are not necessary if both traders and trade unions are against it.

- The holding of insurers Austria Collegialitaet and Bundeslaender due to start on January 1, 1997 plans to strengthen its position abroad. A complete merger following the holding is possible, the chiefs of both companies say.
- Fire engine maker Rosenbauer has received an order from Thailand for 170 fire engines worth 700 million schillings.
- Confectionary maker Manner's turnover rose 12 percent to 523 million schillings in the first half. Exports were up 24 percent in the same period but profits stayed steady.
- Austrian post office savings bank PSK poised to be privatised is about to be changed from a public company to a company limited by shares.
- Die Erste savings bank chief Herbert Schimetschek expects EA-Generali and Die Erste to bid together for the government's stake in Creditanstalt.

- The new British telecommunications giant Concert is the preferred partner for Austria's Post & Telekom Austria. Through an alliance with Tele Denmark the mobile phone unit Mobilkom would also be connected.
- Social Minister Franz Hums wants high income earners to pay more for public health benefits.
- Expanded shop opening hours will create more part-time jobs, however it is expected that this will mean a reduction of full-time jobs.
- Casinos Austria have started a new partnership with the Swiss TSC-group.
- Due to technical problems some banks could not participate in stock exchange transactions at the Vienna bourse on Monday morning.
- A new record for insolvencies of about 320 companies in Austria's ailing construction industry is expected this year.

- Partners in the consortium around EA-Generali bidding for Creditanstalt are prepared to raise their stakes. Germany's Commerzbank would raise its share in the consortium. Die Erste savings bank is also likley to return.
